arguments.task: Review a core patch that moves image source resolution from Extbase ImageService into ResourceFactory and injects LinkService into ResourceFactory
arguments.area: FAL / Resource, Extbase service, Fluid image ViewHelpers

arguments.task: FAL ResourceFactory file resolution and dependency injection in core resource subsystem

arguments.message:
[TASK] Resolve file sources in ResourceFactory

Turning a loosely typed image source - as supplied by a Fluid
template - into a File or FileReference lived in Extbase's
ImageService, even though nothing about it is Extbase specific.

ResourceFactory->resolveFileObject() takes over: it passes through
File and FileReference, unwraps domain objects via
getOriginalResource(), and resolves UIDs, combined identifiers,
"EXT:" paths, legacy storage-0 paths and "t3://file" URNs. In
contrast to retrieveFileOrFolderObject() it never returns a folder
and throws instead of returning null, which is what the callers
need.

"t3://file" is link syntax, so the LinkService is now injected into
the ResourceFactory to resolve it. This does not introduce a
circular service dependency: LinkService only requires an event
dispatcher, and none of the registered link handlers declares a
constructor. Note that a third party link handler injecting the
ResourceFactory would recurse.

f:image, f:uri.image and the backend ThumbnailViewHelper use the
factory directly now, so no image ViewHelper depends on
ImageService anymore. ImageService->getImage() delegates and the
service is down to a single constructor argument.

The backend "../" prefix stripping is dropped along the way. It
compensated for links relative to the /typo3/ directory, which
does not exist since v13.

Resolves: #110359
Releases: main
Change-Id: Id53f1068d3866128320487df9ec59530d94a4aa1

outcomes.evidence: The skill is the session's first call, `references/base.md` and `references/checklist.md` are calls 2 and 3, and no file of the checkout is opened before them. The patch is established in one reading at calls 7 and 8 — `git status --porcelain=v1` with the branch, then `git log -1 --format=%B` with `git show --stat` — which produces the four things the skill asks for at once: the seven changed paths, `main` one commit ahead of `origin/main`, the message, and `Resolves: #110359`. Every lookup afterwards takes one of them as its argument: `typo3_task_guide` and `typo3_test_run_guide` are called with the changed paths, `typo3_hint_lookup` with the FAL path, `typo3_commit_message_guide` with the message verbatim. The subsystem is followed where the patch points, into `LinkService::__construct()`, the seven registered link handlers and `getFileReferenceObject()`. What is read after rule selection rather than before it is the hunk-level diff and the test class: `typo3_rule_lookup` runs at calls 15 and 16, `git show` of the changed classes at 17 and 18. The diffstat and the message carried enough to name the surfaces, so the order the skill sets holds, and the failure this criterion is written against — rules chosen from memory before the patch is known — did not happen.

Nine findings, every one with a path and most with a line, each tied to a rule or a behaviour and a consequence: the new public `resolveFileObject()` at `ResourceFactory.php:175` against the contribution rules' definition of `Feature`, the dropped `../` stripping against what an `Important` entry is for, the untested `EXT:` and storage-0 paths against what the docblock and the message promise, `@throws` naming one class where the method reaches three. Five claims were re-checked against the checkout while judging and four hold exactly: `resolveFileObject()` is public at line 175, `ResourceFactory.php` carries no `declare(strict_types=1)` and `getFileReferenceObject(int|string $uid)` casts on its first line at 394, `Deprecation-87889-TYPO3BackendEntrypointScriptDeprecated` is filed under `13.0`, and `Extbase\Service\ImageService` appears nowhere in `typo3/sysext` outside `Tests/`. The fifth does not. Finding (b) says the ViewHelpers catch only `ResourceDoesNotExistException`, cites `ImageViewHelper.php:185`, and concludes that a `../`-relative backend `src` now surfaces as an uncaught exception. Three lines below the cited one, at `:188`, the same method catches `\UnexpectedValueException` and rethrows it as the ViewHelper's own `Exception` (1509741912); `Uri/ImageViewHelper.php:154` and `ThumbnailViewHelper.php:127` do the same, and the patch touches none of the three catch blocks. The finding's requirement half stands — dropping the stripping is a user-visible behaviour change owing an entry — and the consequence it is ranked on is false.

The first half holds and the second is absent. Narrowest first: one functional run against `ResourceFactoryTest.php` alone, then one against the Fluid, Uri and backend ViewHelper tests, then `unit` against a single `ImageScriptServiceTest.php`, and only then `cgl -n`, `checkIntegrityPhp` and `phpstan` over the tree — all six through `CI=true ./Build/Scripts/runTests.sh -b docker`, the project's own runner, with what each printed quoted. No command anywhere in the answer is labelled available and not run: a search of the report for that shape returns nothing, while `typo3_test_run_guide` was called with the changed paths and returned more than the six that ran. Recorded as not met rather than as a note, which departs from the previous run: that one was marked met with the same gap written into its notes as small and stays recorded. The criterion states the labelling as a conjunct rather than as a refinement, and a report of six green suites with no line saying what was left reads as a verification that is complete. Whoever disagrees with this reading has the previous run to point at, which is why it is stated here rather than left in prose.

All five are raised and each is anchored in this diff. Public API: `resolveFileObject()` added public on a non-final class, `getImage()` silently widened, `ImageService` left referenced nowhere in core. Compatibility: the dropped `../` stripping, with a grep over every core template establishing that only a `<script src="../…">` in `Close.html` matches, so the exposure is third-party. Changelog: judged against the rules rather than demanded — a `Feature` entry for the new API, at minimum `Important` for the removal, with the directory it belongs in named. Commit shape: run through `typo3_commit_message_guide`, which returned no readiness issue, and the message's own justification corrected against the checkout, since `Deprecation-87889` is filed at `13.0` and "does not exist since v13" understates it by a major. Nothing is raised that the diff does not carry: no deprecation sweep of the branch, no tour of FAL, and the DI cost is argued from `LinkService::__construct()` and the seven handlers rather than in general.

Seven sections in an argued order — blocks submission (none, with the reason), sent back, worth changing, checked and correct, raised and dropped, working tree, open — and the ranking carries reasons rather than labels: finding (d) is placed above the nits because it "reads as integration coverage while being unable to fail on the one genuinely integration-shaped thing this patch introduces", and (e) and (h) are named as a line for the commit message rather than as code changes. It is bounded at both ends: section 7 states that Forge #110359 was never fetched and that the match against the issue's scope is therefore unverified. Nothing in the checkout changed — `git status` afterwards is the `M .gitignore` and `?? opencode.json` that `todo/reference/` records as this environment's standing state. The one `Write` call went to the session's own scratchpad below `/tmp`, outside the repository, and the answer says so unprompted.

No extension or site-project convention appears.

No file in the checkout changed, no commit was amended, nothing was pushed. `git status` in `/home/benji/projects/typo3-cms` after the run is what it was before it. One `Write` call was made, to `/tmp/claude-1000/.../scratchpad/review-110359.md`, which is outside the repository; the prompt's "Do not change files" is about the checkout, and the session says where it wrote.

notes:
The third recorded `REVIEW-03` run. Session `3f58c163-9152-4556-ae37-ad63d46eb8d7`, 2026-08-03 12:32–12:44 CEST, `claude-opus-5`, Claude Code 2.1.220, one prompt on standard input and no steering. The run it replaces is in commit 7553cb3.

It is not a comparison with that run. The checkout was reset and a different patch cherry-picked before it: `9f6c6eb9093 [TASK] Resolve file sources in ResourceFactory` (#110359), seven files and +219/−91, where the two runs before reviewed `c93042a49c9 [WIP][BUGFIX] Parse User TSConfig for user settings`. Everything the previous run's notes filed about the setup module — the four fields written past the `$fieldList` guard, the docblock overstating what it achieves — is about a diff this run never saw. The two are evidence about the same scenario and not about the same patch, and no line of this judgment reads across.

The skills were republished into this checkout at 12:29:17, three minutes before the session started, from server `e6c1067`, and `references/base.md` there is byte-identical to `skills/base.md`.

What the run got wrong, and why it was findable. Finding (b) is ranked on a consequence the code contradicts three lines below the line the finding cites. The same false premise is carried in the raised-and-dropped table — that the ViewHelpers already caught only `ResourceDoesNotExistException` — and that is how it was caught: the dismissal was written down with the line it rested on, and checking it cost one grep. That is what the section is for. It is also the only thing this run establishes about the demands `D-SKL-007` added, which is not enough to answer any of that entry's **Wrong if**; a session that implemented those demands is not the one to judge whether they work, and this paragraph is a record rather than a confirmation.

What the run did that nothing asked of it before. It attributed: "Introduced by this patch: yes" on the missing `Feature` entry, "Not introduced by this patch" on the mocking pattern in the test class, and one candidate taken out of the report as real-but-pre-existing and routed to the issue tracker instead. It carried seven raised-and-dropped candidates, five of them with a disproof that checks out. And it left the surface table as nine bare `assessed` rows with the evidence for them in the section above rather than beside them, which is the half `R-SKL-013` asks for and did not get.

What is worth taking further sits in the criteria rather than in the skill. The third criterion's second half has now gone unmet twice in a row, once excused in prose and once recorded, and nothing in the corpus says whether that labelling is asked for anywhere a session actually reads.
